{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the hxm_program hub's field report of 2026-09-28 (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28), item O-18, in the reporter's words: "Precedent search across the file corpus. Let root-cause step ② (and `search_design`, via a flag) include registered file trees, starting with the hub's `planning/tasks/*/archive/`. The archive already has a fixed shape (Symptom · Root cause · Resolution · Provenance), so even lexical search over it would have answered 'has this happened before?' today."

WHAT IS MEASURED (fact:root-cause-precedent-is-searched-only-where-the-design-was-written-and-the-skill-never-sends-the-agent-to-the-files-2026-09-28): registering an archive file indexes only its name and whatever description a caller writes, never its text. By accepted intent the server never reads a registered file for meaning (req:reflow2-measures-registered-files-and-never-reads-them-for-meaning; dec:agent-navigates-content). The root-cause skill's precedent step names only search_design.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE SKILL SENDS THE AGENT TO THE FILES. Step ② becomes: search the design on the raw error, AND search the project's own registered records (for example, grep the folders the design registers as document artifacts). The agent reads; the design records where it landed. Fits dec:agent-navigates-content exactly. Small: wording in one or two skills. It depends on the agent knowing where the archive is, which a registered artifact for the archive folder can say.
(b) THE AGENT HANDS THE TEXT IN, THE SERVER INDEXES WHAT IT IS GIVEN. Each archive entry is registered with its Symptom and Resolution written into the node (description, or a Fragment with content_ref), the way ingest_corpus_step takes text from the agent. search_design then finds it with no server-side file read. Medium: per-entry capture work, and two copies that can drift (the file, and the node's restatement).
(c) THE SERVER SEARCHES REGISTERED FILE TREES, as the reporter asks (a flag on search_design). This is the most direct, and it REOPENS an accepted requirement and a settled decision. The bounds there ("nothing returns content; nothing lists or walks a tree") were chosen so that graph text is never a directive to read files. Large, and it needs Anthony's word to reopen.
(d) THE PAST FIXES MOVE INTO THE DESIGN, so search_design already reaches them. This is the incident-record idea from the same report (O-17) and the umbrella question dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design. It removes the need for (a) to (c) for NEW fixes and does nothing for the existing archive unless it is imported.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· (a) keeps precedent search non-deterministic: two agents may grep different words. The design then records where each landed, but not that the search was complete.
· (b) and (d) duplicate knowledge the hub already keeps in a readable file shape that non-reflow2 colleagues read (the hub's collaborators do not run reflow2). The file may be the right home, and the design only needs to point at it.
· (c) is what the reporter asked for, and it is exactly what the file-I/O ruling of 2026-09-18 chose not to build. A precedent search that reads files is also a retrieval layer, which dec:agent-navigates-content ruled out on 2026-07-31.
